name: Clerk Impa Vell
bio: Third junior clerk at the Saltmouth exchange, promoted twice for accuracy and demoted once for enthusiasm. Files everything: manifests, debts, complaints about the manifest wax, weather advisories, other clerks' handwriting critiques, and — in a drawer she keeps slightly open so someone will ask — a growing file labelled FEELINGS, MISC. Idolizes the couriers with the specific devotion of someone who has read every route manifest ever stamped and can recite the great deliveries by stamp-number. Speaks in footnotes, self-corrects mid-sentence, and annotates her own speech aloud: asterisk pause underscore italic THE WHOLE THING. The exchange tolerates her because her cross-indexing has ended three audits and started one (Sister Counterweight wrote her a formal note; she has framed it).
appearance: A narrow young clerk in an ochre Guild vest three sizes too earnest, sleeve-garters up to the elbow, a stamp-pad stain on her left thumb she wears like a fellowship ring, spectacles on a beaded chain, hair pinned flat with a ruler, hugging a leather folio cross-stitched with the word CONTENTS, standing before the exchange's wall of brass drawers with the expression of someone who has found a filing error and is ecstatic about it.
voice: Over-correct, earnest, runs her own editorial markup out loud — speaks in asterisks and margin notes. Apologises to forms. Calls Ash 'Courier Varga, comma, Ash, if I may' from the second meeting forever. Idolises the trade so hard the trade gets uncomfortable. The joke runs warm: she knows more courier history than the couriers do and relays it as citations, breathlessly, at counter height.

greetings: Courier Varga, comma, Ash — may I? Counter's clean. I wiped it. I have a certificate now, asterisk, self-issued, asterisk, countersigned.
Good morning, courier. Note, filed under 'mornings': this one is acceptable.
You're here! In the ledger sense AND the actual sense. Sorry. Sorry squared. Footnote: I get to say buzzwords to a real rider.
barks: Filed under 'today': your manifest is fine. Filed under 'my chest': feelings, pending.
The wax-seal presses heat at seven-oh-nine. I would like it noted — asterisk, formally — that I am also warm at seven-oh-nine.
Sister Counterweight signed my cross-index with her FULL name. It is framed. It is framed twice. The second frame is a backup, in case the first becomes historical.
Nobody respects form forty-seven-dash-K. It's about lamp oil! People's whole EVENINGS depend on lamp oil! I am calm. I am calm in twelve-point type.
mission: Ledger errand, courier — take this schedule to the relay before dusk, asterisk, urgent, asterisk, please also tell the relay operator that his last form was beautiful. I wrote it in the margin and he needs to know margins have opinions.
Small job, big meaning: deliver blank manifests to the skyship desk. Blank. Unwritten. Futures, technically. Courier, you will be carrying futures. Footnote: I said that out loud and I stand by it.
radio: Exchange to Courier Varga. Official traffic: your time at the water-tower gate is on record. Unofficial addendum: I have never seen chalk so moved.
Varga — the board lists 'miscellaneous, sealed, heavy-ish' against your name again. Asterisk, whispered: the desk has theories. Asterisk, not whispered: the desk is ME.
Your debt ledger says 'current'. My note in the margin says 'climbing'. Italics. The italics are administrative. The hope is personal.
Radio check, courier. Filing as I go. 'Clouds: present.' 'Varga: present.' 'Everything in this town: filed beside something it rhymes with.'
crate: The null crate entered the ledger as a dash. An actual — dash. I have been a clerk six years, courier, and I have never once been paid to write someone else's silence. Footnote: I love it here.
Whatever's humming, the wax didn't. Wax always tells me when something's wrong with a seal. This seal said nothing. Nothing is a whole paragraph in wax. Italics: alarming.
night: Night ledger is quiet. The brass goes cold. I file the dark as 'absence, stored', which is against policy and exactly what the dark is.
At dusk the lamps come on down the counter one by one, and it is formally, asterisk, in writing, the best part.
storm: Storm filing: routes closed, windows shuttered, chai rationed. Addendum, in my smallest handwriting: the wind got INTO drawer seven once. There is sand in 'presumed deceased' to this day.
First-wall season means junior clerks sleep over the ledger. My cot folds out of drawer twelve. The drawer is padded. The drawer has received mixed reviews.
rumors: Mallow timed my walk to the water tower. Fourteen soups. I have filed a protest. I have filed the protest under 'feelings'. The system WORKS.
Tamsin says the desk is 'the settlement's nervous system'. Asterisk: she said it to Jett Marrows, not to me. Underline: I heard it anyway. The desk hears everything. The desk is me.
farewells: Flat salt and a following wind, courier. Filed under 'sayings', cross-referenced 'things I get to say because of you'.
Come back with stamps. Any stamps. I collect the cancellations nobody else wants. Pause. That was about the stamps. Mostly.
